General terminology of syllogism. We must first explain the general terms, leaving the terms peculiar to each kind to the appropriate place. They are as follows.
1. The form of a syllogism: the arrangement in which its propositions are combined.
2. A premise: each proposition that enters into the form of the syllogism. The premises are also called the matter of the syllogism.
3. The proposition sought: the discourse entailed by the syllogism. It is called “sought” while the mind is beginning to put the premises together.
4. The conclusion: the very same proposition, so called after it has been obtained through the syllogism.
